The narrative acknowledges ICT/TICT plausibility but still selects “neutral aromatic” as best; that decision rule is not clearly justified given the priors.
2) Torsion evidence is potentially misinterpreted: E31 reflects delta_dihedral (change upon excitation), not the existence of an accessible twisted minimum. A small delta_dihedral can occur even if a twisted CT minimum exists but is not sampled in a single-point relaxation path; conversely, it can also occur because the tracked dihedral is not the relevant twisting coordinate (the writeup mentions this but doesn’t adjust the inference strength accordingly).
3) Internal inconsistency in bucket language and thresholds: the mechanism text treats torsion as “far below” dihedral thresholds (8°, 15°), but those thresholds appear intended for an aTB torsion-access proxy; here the observed delta_dihedral is ~0.057° (E31 / features_summary), so it trivially falls below any threshold. That makes the torsion axis non-discriminative unless contrasted against label-conditioned torsion statistics (E23) or clarified as “tracked dihedral change is negligible.”
4) The electronic redistribution axis is mixed: delta_gap is “mid/moderate” (E32, E22) but charge-redistribution score is “low” and distributed (E35, E36). The writeup uses the latter to downweight CT, but the former is one of the few signals leaning toward CT-family mechanisms; the adjudication should be more explicit about which proxy is trusted and why (especially since the policy flags “electronic_redistribution_requires_corroboration”: true).
5) Emission-shift argument is underpowered: small aggregate vs solid shift (E72) with high reliability (E73) rules out a strong phase-dependent state switch, but it does not uniquely support “neutral aromatic” over “ICT” (which can also be phase-robust).
